- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.20), model tends to overestimate mean reversion; cap forecast at 1-2% above recent 10-day average to avoid overcorrection.  
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., > 0.30), model often underestimates rally; add 2-5% buffer to forecast tail end to capture momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.30+ swings); apply 3-5% upward bias to 30d forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.30.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model often fails to capture early recovery; add 1-3% upward bias to forecast 10-15 days ahead of recovery window.
